review.tagline: Embeddable local microVM sandboxes for running untrusted code and AI agents
review.summary: Microsandbox boots OCI images (Docker Hub, GHCR, any registry) as hardware-isolated microVMs, with reported average boot times under 100 ms. It ships an `msb` CLI and SDKs for TypeScript, Rust, Python, Go and Ruby that spawn VMs as child processes, with no server or daemon. It supports forking live sandboxes, snapshots, network allowlists and secrets that never enter the VM. The README marks it as beta software.
review.audience: Developers isolating AI agent or user-submitted code in local microVMs
strengths: Embeddable SDKs spawn microVMs in-process; no setup server or long-running daemon
Fork running sandboxes and snapshot or restore full state
Runs standard OCI images on Linux (KVM), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows (WHP)
Secrets stay outside the VM; network access limited by host allowlist
weaknesses: README warns of beta status: breaking changes, missing features, rough edges
Needs KVM on Linux, Apple Silicon on macOS, or WHP on Windows
First create() pulls the image, so initial start depends on network
Intel Macs are not listed as supported
needs: Needs KVM (Linux), WHP (Windows), OCI registry access
